definitions.explanation: Freedom from guilt or wrongdoing, especially in legal or accusatory contexts. Used when someone is cleared of suspicion or asserts they have done nothing wrong.
Moral cleanliness and integrity of character. Describes a person who is honest and free from corruption.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{潔白|けっぱく}を{主張|しゅちょう}した。
{調査|ちょうさ}の{結果|けっか}、{彼|かれ}の{潔白|けっぱく}が{証明|しょうめい}された。
examples.english: As a result of the investigation, his innocence was proven.

examples.japanese: {疑|うたが}いをかけられても、{自分|じぶん}の{潔白|けっぱく}を{信|しん}じて{堂々|どうどう}としていた。
examples.english: Even when accused, he stood firm believing in his own innocence.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{潔白|けっぱく}な{人柄|ひとがら}で{知|し}られている。
examples.english: He is known for his upright character.

examples.japanese: {政治家|せいじか}には{潔白|けっぱく}さが{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: Politicians are expected to have integrity.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}にわたって{潔白|けっぱく}な{態度|たいど}を{貫|つらぬ}いてきた{役人|やくにん}は{市民|しみん}から{信頼|しんらい}されている。
examples.english: The official who has maintained an upright attitude over many years is trusted by the citizens.

notes:
USAGE:
Most frequently used in sense 1 (innocence), particularly in the phrase {潔白|けっぱく}を{証明|しょうめい}する (prove one's innocence). Sense 2 (moral purity) is more literary.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {潔白|けっぱく}を{証明|しょうめい}する (prove one's innocence)
- {潔白|けっぱく}を{主張|しゅちょう}する (assert one's innocence)
- {潔白|けっぱく}な{身|み} (a clean/innocent person)
- {身|み}の{潔白|けっぱく} (one's innocence)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無罪|むざい}: not guilty — a legal verdict, used in court
- {無実|むじつ}: innocence — specifically means falsely accused, did not commit the act
- {清廉|せいれん}: incorruptible — a more formal/literary word for moral integrity
